evidence.claim: Cached Layer 2 identifies data-center power infrastructure, electrical switchgear, grid and power bottlenecks, data-center thermal infrastructure, liquid cooling, and construction-execution capacity as relevant AI infrastructure nodes.

Cached Layer 2 states that reports of lead-time extension, allocation, or price increases in advanced materials and equipment would be direct bottleneck confirmation signals; by inference, similar lead-time, backlog, and pricing evidence is relevant for power, thermal, switchgear, and grid-interconnect nodes.

Cached Layer 2 treats customer pre-funding, capacity reservation, backlog conversion, and qualification/certification as important evidence types for determining whether an upstream supply-chain node is strategic rather than commodity procurement.

The candidate chunk identifies Modine as a mid-cap thermal-management and heat-transfer company whose key verification path is whether data-center thermal revenue, orders, and margins are becoming material and whether products are exposed to liquid cooling rather than only conventional HVAC.

The candidate chunk identifies Powell Industries as a mid-cap electrical distribution, switchgear, and power-control company whose key verification path is whether backlog, customer mix, and margin expansion are tied to data-center or grid-interconnect demand.

The candidate chunk identifies MYR Group as a small-cap electrical construction and transmission/distribution services company whose key verification path is whether data-center-related transmission, distribution, and substation work is visible in backlog and margins.

The candidate chunk identifies Siltronic as a mid-cap silicon-wafer supplier with a second-order AI semiconductor materials thesis linked to leading-edge wafer demand, high-purity inputs, and long-term contract quality.

External search context included an investor presentation from SUSS MicroTec describing the company as a hidden champion semiconductor frontend and advanced-backend equipment supplier benefiting from AI and advanced packaging demand, but SUSS is not part of the visible candidate chunk and is therefore not ranked here.

External search context included a Seeking Alpha article describing Arteris as a hidden AI hyperscaler beneficiary through NoC interconnect IP, but Arteris is not part of the visible candidate chunk and is therefore not ranked here.
evidence.source_title: Arteris Stock: A Hidden Beneficiary Of Hyperscaler AI Spending

memory_update.content: For AI infrastructure Layer 3 scoring, prioritize underfollowed small/mid-cap candidates when they combine durable demand, a clear physical or qualification bottleneck, and a falsifiable evidence path through backlog, segment mix, margins, customer mix, or product-level disclosures.
Promote MOD, POWL, MYRG, AAON, and NVT to the next verification layer for data-center thermal, switchgear, grid-interconnect, cooling, and electrical-protection nodes.

Use VRT, ETN, and FIX as reference leaders for power, electrical infrastructure, thermal systems, and construction-execution bottlenecks, but do not let their popularity crowd out underfollowed suppliers.

Downgrade candidates if filings and earnings calls fail to show material data-center exposure, backlog conversion, margin improvement, customer qualification, or pricing power tied to AI infrastructure rather than ordinary industrial, HVAC, construction, or semiconductor cycles.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether data-center thermal revenue, orders, and margins are becoming material and whether products are exposed to liquid cooling rather than only conventional HVAC.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need company filings, earnings-call transcripts, segment disclosures, backlog commentary, and customer/product evidence showing that AI data-center thermal demand is material and not merely a small narrative overlay.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Modine ranks first because high-density AI data centers create a durable thermal-management demand driver, and the company may have a more direct liquid-cooling and heat-transfer exposure than its legacy industrial/HVAC label implies. The thesis is testable through data-center thermal revenue, orders, margins, product mix, and evidence that liquid or hybrid cooling is becoming material.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It can be screened as an industrial heat-transfer or HVAC company rather than as a beneficiary of AI rack-density and data-center cooling constraints.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether backlog, customer mix, and margin expansion are tied to data-center or grid interconnect demand rather than oil, gas, petrochemical, or general industrial cycles.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need backlog composition, customer-end-market mix, order commentary, and margin bridge evidence separating data-center/grid-related strength from legacy industrial-cycle strength.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Powell scores highly because AI data centers require switchgear, power-control, and electrical-distribution equipment, and these nodes can become practical bottlenecks when utility interconnect and power-delivery projects accelerate. Its industrial classification may obscure a potentially meaningful data-center power-infrastructure signal.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It may screen primarily as an oil, gas, petrochemical, or industrial electrical-equipment supplier rather than as a data-center power bottleneck candidate.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether data-center-related transmission, distribution, and substation work is visible in backlog and margins.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need concrete disclosure tying backlog growth, project awards, customer mix, or margin expansion to data-center interconnection, utility upgrade, or substation work.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: MYR Group is a high-priority underfollowed candidate because grid interconnect, transmission, distribution, and substation work can become second-order bottlenecks for AI data-center energization. The small-cap profile and low AI mindshare improve discovery value, while backlog and margin disclosures provide a clear evidence path.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is usually viewed as an electrical contractor or utility-infrastructure services company, not as a direct AI data-center beneficiary.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether data-center orders, backlog, and gross margins are accelerating and whether the company has exposure to AI-driven liquid or hybrid cooling.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence that data-center demand is both material and differentiated, especially whether AI rack-density requirements are improving mix or margins versus standard commercial HVAC demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: AAON has a plausible AI data-center thermal angle because specialized cooling demand should rise with data-center expansion and higher rack densities. The opportunity is less clearly bottlenecked than liquid-cooling-specialist or power-equipment nodes, but it has a straightforward test through orders, backlog, gross margin, and product mix.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It may be perceived mainly as an HVAC manufacturer rather than a supplier to high-density data-center thermal infrastructure.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether data-center and high-density electrical infrastructure are large enough within segment revenue and backlog to drive differentiated growth.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need clearer quantification of data-center revenue, backlog, product mix, and whether high-density AI infrastructure is improving growth or margins beyond ordinary industrial demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: nVent is less pure than the top mid-cap candidates but remains attractive for Layer 3 because enclosures, electrical protection, and connection systems may benefit from higher-density data-center power and thermal infrastructure. Its evidence path is clean: segment mix, data-center backlog, high-density product commentary, and margins.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Its AI exposure is embedded inside broader industrial and electrical categories rather than obvious AI infrastructure labels.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether incremental backlog and margins are still driven by data-center work and whether labor capacity, project timing, or customer concentration create bottleneck economics.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need updated backlog, margin, labor-capacity, customer-concentration, and project-timing evidence to determine whether bottleneck economics remain incremental or already priced.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Comfort Systems USA remains important as a benchmark for construction-execution bottlenecks in data-center mechanical, electrical, and plumbing work. It ranks below more hidden candidates because the AI data-center construction thesis appears more widely recognized, reducing underfollowed-discovery and mispricing scores.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not strongly underfollowed at this stage; included as a reference leader for data-center construction and execution capacity.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether data-center customer exposure is material enough to offset nonresidential construction cycles and commodity-linked margin pressure.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need end-market disclosure showing data-center exposure is material, durable, and margin-accretive rather than overwhelmed by commodity pricing and general construction cyclicality.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Atkore is a credible underfollowed candidate because data-center construction requires conduit, raceway, and electrical infrastructure products. However, bottleneck severity and supplier scarcity are less obvious than in switchgear, grid interconnect, or specialized thermal systems, and commodity-linked margin pressure may dilute the AI signal.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is typically viewed as a construction and electrical-products company rather than a data-center supply-chain beneficiary.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether leading-edge wafer demand and input constraints improve pricing, utilization, or long-term contract quality.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence that leading-edge or AI-related wafer demand is improving pricing, utilization, contract duration, or customer behavior, rather than a general semiconductor inventory cycle.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Siltronic has a plausible second-order AI semiconductor materials angle because silicon wafers sit below leading-edge chip manufacturing and depend on constrained high-purity inputs. It ranks mid-pack because the direct AI linkage is less immediate than data-center power or thermal nodes, and wafer cyclicality may dominate near-term fundamentals.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It can be overlooked in AI screens because it appears as a cyclical wafer supplier rather than part of the AI semiconductor capacity stack.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether order growth, liquid cooling mix, pricing, backlog conversion, and margins remain strong enough to justify its reference-leader status.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need current order, backlog, pricing, liquid-cooling mix, and margin evidence to judge whether the reference-leader thesis is still strengthening or already fully reflected.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Vertiv has one of the strongest direct exposures to AI data-center power and thermal infrastructure, but it is treated as a reference leader rather than an underfollowed discovery. Its high fundamental relevance is offset by lower mispricing and discovery scores because the market already associates the company with AI infrastructure.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included to benchmark smaller suppliers against a recognized power and thermal infrastructure leader.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether data-center-driven electrical demand is incremental versus already priced, and whether smaller suppliers show stronger or weaker bottleneck economics.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need updated data-center backlog, electrical segment pricing, capacity commentary, and margin evidence to separate incremental AI demand from already-recognized electrification themes.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Eaton is a useful benchmark for data-center electrical distribution, power management, switchgear, and grid-related infrastructure demand. It ranks below underfollowed candidates because it is a large, well-covered reference company with broad end-market exposure and less hidden-discovery value.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included as a benchmark for electrical-infrastructure pricing, order strength, and margin expectations.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether AI/cloud-driven asset sprawl is translating into faster billings, net retention, platform consolidation, or pricing power.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need stronger evidence that AI infrastructure expansion is specifically driving Tenable’s financial metrics, rather than general cybersecurity budget trends or competitive replacement cycles.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Tenable is included but ranked lower because AI/cloud asset sprawl is a plausible cybersecurity demand driver, not yet a clear Serenity-style physical or qualification bottleneck. The thesis may become more interesting if billings, net retention, platform consolidation, or pricing power show direct acceleration from cloud and AI infrastructure complexity.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It may be missed in AI infrastructure screens because it is a cybersecurity and exposure-management software company rather than a hardware, data-center, or semiconductor supplier.

summary: This Layer 3 ranking favors underfollowed, testable supply-chain nodes tied to AI data-center power, thermal, grid-interconnect, and semiconductor input bottlenecks. The top priorities are Modine, Powell Industries, MYR Group, AAON, and nVent because they sit one or two layers below obvious AI compute demand and have clear falsification paths through backlog, segment mix, margins, customer disclosures, and order commentary. Reference leaders such as Vertiv, Eaton, and Comfort Systems USA remain useful benchmarks but receive lower underfollowed-discovery and mispricing scores because the market already recognizes their AI infrastructure exposure.
